The theme of this meeting is step study for recovery and healing from harmfully intertwined work and activity related compulsions linked with abuse, trauma, abandonment and neglect in early life. We meet weekly and study a step a month. As adult children recovering from workaholism, it is our group conscience to use literature from ACA as well as WA. The meeting itself includes program readings, brief meditation, time for writing on step questions, and sharing based on the step of that month. There may be silence on the line if you call in during the writing period. We also provide guidelines for deeper exploration of additional step reading and writing for those who would like to do that, which could be with a step buddy, between meetings. This meeting is 1 hour and 15 minutes long.

notes:
The Rule 62 Group meets every Thursday at 7:00 pm until 8:30 pm, in the building behind St. Paul's Episcopal Church.
It is a non-smoking meeting with a coffee/smoke break. Wheelchair accessible.
The 1st Thursday of every month is a book study.
We read from the Dual Disorders Recovery Book and share as we go on how it relates to us.
On the 3rd Thursday of every month, we read from the 12 steps and Dual disorders Book and share or ask questions about what we read.
All other Thursdays are open for participation. We are a closed meeting for DRA members only,  BUT .... If you suspect you might have a mood or psychiatric disorder And chemical dependency, you are welcome to attend.
For more info: 
Steve (661) 916- 5410

name: Grieving Without The Green
notes:
This is a meeting specifically designed for marijuana addicts that are dealing with aspects of grief and loss as well as their addiction to Cannabis. It is a common thing among addicts that when we are confronted by grief and especially loss in our lives, these events can often cue up strong desires to use in order to get through the deep sadness. This vulnerable state can then trigger a relapse, compounding our difficulties. We are here for the marijuana addict facing these strong emotions and challenges. Through supportive discussion, MA literature as well as other resource study, and speakers who themselves have traversed these difficult waters of recovery, we will share our Experience, Strength, and Hope with each other as we recover from what is often one of life's most difficult chapters.

Email: GrievingWOTG@gmail.com

name: Grieving Without The Green
notes:
This is a meeting specifically designed for marijuana addicts that are dealing with aspects of grief and loss as well as their addiction to Cannabis. It is a common thing among addicts that when we are confronted by grief and especially loss in our lives, these events can often cue up strong desires to use in order to get through the deep sadness. This vulnerable state can then trigger a relapse, compounding our difficulties. We are here for the marijuana addict facing these strong emotions and challenges. Through supportive discussion, MA literature as well as other resource study, and speakers who themselves have traversed these difficult waters of recovery, we will share our Experience, Strength, and Hope with each other as we recover from what is often one of life's most difficult chapters.

Email: GrievingWOTG@gmail.com

Sydney based, all locations welcome.
Closed Meetings are open only to those individuals who have a desire to stop their addictive sexual behaviour.
Open Meetings are open to anyone interested in finding out about SAA; those who attend need not have admitted that their sexual behavior is a problem.
Online meetings are only actively running with a host as per the above schedule.

notes:

This is a closed meeting for ACAs including Double Winner, Newcomers, and the LGBTQ Community. You must be logged into your Zoom account to join (Zoom Authenticated). Thank you, and Mabuhay. The Buo meeting will last for 60 minutes. In our Mabuhay meetings - we invite people to speak and share in any language they are comfortable with. In our perspective - the language of recovery and love is universal. Listening and sharing are part of service. Your presence and voices are all welcome. ()

name: Life of Love: Living a Spiritually Sustainable Lifestyle WEB1496
notes:
Meeting ID: 863 6061 6895 Passcode: 1234 Virtual Meeting Link This is a non-traditional ACA meeting dedicated to nurturing a spiritually sustainable recovery lifestyle. Each month - we explore an ACA recovery topic in combination with an external practice or tool—such as somatic work - creative expression - spiritual rituals - trauma-informed care - diet - plant-based healing - and other lifestyle practices. - - We ground our shares in ACA principles and literature while welcoming personal experience with outside tools. This meeting is inclusive of members in multi-program recovery who draw from a range of practices to heal - regulate - and grow. - - Our format includes conference approved literature readings - workshop questions - brief meditations/reflections - and open sharing. We also host a monthly speaker meeting. Members are encouraged to share from their personal experience and avoid giving advice or prescribing tools. - - This meeting uses both conference-approved and non-conference-approved content to support deeper reflection and sustainable daily routines. We respect the diversity of recovery paths and hold space for the unfolding of each person’s healing journey with humility - curiosity - and care. (English)

notes:
ROOM OPENS 15 MINUTES PRIOR TO START Virtual Meeting Link Saturday 09:00 AM WEB1019 Secular Serenity Saturday - - - - Each month - we are working on a different 12 Step with interpretations from a source outside of ACA literature. ACA accommodates outside literature if the meeting is based on ACA's Traditions. The author's name and a URL to their work will be provided in the meeting. This group meets every Saturday. - - The Zoom information is the SAME for ALL Agnostics ACA meetings. All information on how to access the meeting is below the meeting description. This is a weekly Agnostic ACA secular meeting. - - - - - - Agnostics ACA is open to everyone. If you are atheist - agnostic - a freethinker - humanist - uncomfortable with the religious language in ACA literature - questioning what Higher Power means to you - or simply looking for a new meeting - then this group might be for you. We are not angry atheists or against a Higher Power. We believe in personal accountability and that ACA recovery can be successful with or without “god.” We acknowledge a Judeo/Christian Higher Power does not work for everyone. notes: The Zoom information is the SAME for ALL AgnosticACA meetings. All information on how to access the meeting is below the meeting description. AgnosticACA is open to everyone in ACA. name: Dragons to Slay - S.L.A.A. Study Meeting for Fantasy Addicts
notes:
Are you in need of tools to take the next step in your fight against addictive fantasy? The Fantasy Writing Group (FWG for short, a subcommittee of the S.L.A.A. Conference Member Retention Committee) is chartered with the task of creating new draft literature on the topic of fantasy addiction for consideration as Conference Approved Literature in S.L.A.A. The FWG has created a set of study questions specifically for fantasy addicts to go with each of these tools:
 
 
 The Characteristics of Fantasy Addiction 
 The Steps 
 The Signs of Recovery from Fantasy Addiction 
 
 
 The Dragons to Slay fantasy study meeting is designed to explore our answers to each of these questions as a way to deepen our recovery by understanding the role fantasy plays in our sex and love addiction and the tools we can develop to take contrary action.
 
 The Dragons to Slay meeting is different than other S.L.A.A. meetings. In order to maximize the number of answers to the fantasy addiction study questions we get to hear in 60 minutes, we do not do the normal beginning- or end-of-meeting S.L.A.A. readings, nor do we do introductions or a Seventh Tradition break. After the opening Serenity Prayer and guidelines for sharing, we go directly into the questions we have selected for the week and start sharing our answers (in the order we have raised our virtual hands) in three-minute shares. Shares are restricted to answers to the questions or experiences that are related to the study questions being answe

name: S.L.A.A. New Beginnings telephone
notes:
S.L.A.A. New Beginnings: EVERY DAY 3:00 P.M. EST / 12:00 P.M. PST
Open Meeting (Anyone Can Attend)
 This meeting uses varied formats each day of the week to explore our sex and love addiction. By group conscience, the subjects for each day are:
 
 Sundays: Fantasy Addiction 
 Mondays: A State of Grace 
 Tuesdays: Top and Bottom Lines 
 Wednesdays: Healthy Relationships 
 Thursdays: Obsession 
 Fridays: Triggers as a Resource 
 Saturdays: Newcomers meeting 
 
 SUNDAYS: The Sunday edition of the daily New Beginnings meeting is focused on how an addiction to fantasy enables and even super-charges our larger sex and love addiction. The meeting reads from S.L.A.A. literature on the topic of compulsive fantasy, including draft literature in front of the Fellowship, as well as articles from S.L.A.A.'s bi-monthly publication theJournal on fantasy. 
 MONDAYS : The Monday edition of the daily New Beginnings meeting reads from the S.L.A.A. daily meditation reader, A State of Grace . The meeting encourages shares guided by that day's reading, though getting current or sharing on anything that aids participants in their recovery is welcome.
 TUESDAYS : The Tuesday edition of the daily New Beginnings meeting is focused on the topic of setting and maintaining Top and Bottom Lines. The meeting reads from the "Setting Bottom Lines" pamphlet and from articles in S.L.A.A.'s bi-monthly publication theJournal in editions dedicated to the topics of Top Lines and Bottom Lines.
 WEDNESDAYS : The Wed

name: SLAA HOW Meeting (Video ON)
notes:
SLAA HOW Meeting (Video ON).
 Join Zoom Meeting: https://zoom.us/j/7834184169 Passkey: 1
 We welcome all Newcomers and Old Timers in SLAA.
 Our meeting is open to all participants – video should be ON and fellows visible at all times with appropriate lighting and clothing. Appropriate behaviour is requested at all times*.
 The format of the meeting alternates each week:
 Step Discussion – We read a step from the SLAA Basic Text and share back on our experience or understanding of that step.
 Chair – A SLAA member shares their experience, strength, and hope of addiction and recovery. Here we respond to the Chair and/or get current.
 Note: all meetings invite members to get current on what is going on for them.
 We have an online fellowship after every meeting. All are welcome to stay behind post meeting.
 The meeting size usually allows everyone who wishes to share the opportunity. We welcome people of any gender, sexuality, race, or background who have a desire to stop living out a pattern of sex and love addiction.
 Newcomers are especially welcome!
 *It is very important to us that people behave in the Zoom meeting as if they are at an actual meeting - visible with camera on, appropriate clothing, little movement, no eating, smoking, no lying in bed, no driving around, etc. This is all said in a safety statement in the meeting.

Meeting ID: 981 878 1190Password: HLNC
What is body doubling? It could be step work, housework, or anything. It’s a tool to help people who have trouble focusing on a task when completely alone (because of distracting thoughts and feelings) come together and have a form of soft accountability in the shape of another person also working alongside them. Think of a group of students all working on homework together—they might all be taking different classes and working on different subjects but when they are sitting together and working there’s less temptation for procrastination.

 Divorce with Dignity is a Group of SLAA members supporting one another to apply the principles of Sex and Love Addicts Anonymous recovery program to navigate their divorce in a dignified manner.
 In SLAA we develop self-respect, sobriety, and spiritual principles through our Twelve Step program which is how we:
1 manage emotions,
2 set boundaries, and
3 foster a sense of inner wholeness,
during the difficult divorce process.
 Our shared goal is to restore our personal dignity, regardless of the circumstances of the marriage or divorce.
 We apply these SLAA principles: 
 Sobriety: 
Practicing daily abstinence from acting out in a way that causes harm to oneself or others provides a foundation of personal choice and dignity.
 Sellf-Inventory and Amends: 
The Twelve Steps encourage a self-inventory of wrongs and a willingness to make amends, fostering personal responsibility and self-awareness during divorce.
 Spirituality: 
Developing a relationship with a Higher Power can provide guidance and strength to cope with the emotional turmoil of divorce.
 Dignity of Self: 
The SLAA recovery process emphasizes finding wholeness and dignity within oneself, which is crucial for maintaining self-respect during a marriage ending.

While this meeting is not exclusively for Minor Attracted Persons (MAPs) and any individual wanting to recover from sex and love addiction may attend our meetings, participants must maintain a safe, confidential space for MAPs to share.

Our meetings are intended to provide minor-attracted people with a safe place to share their experience, strength, and hope with one another as we walk the path of recovery. Whatever the nature of your struggle, if you feel our meetings could be a safe place for you to share, you belong here.

name: Christian Focus Workshop
notes:
Christian Focus ZOOM Workshop This meeting is camera-optional We read from a trauma informed Christian book: Unmasking the Monster, Shining the Light of God’s Word on Abuse (2025), by Shawn Foster (2025). While this is a Christian-based book, you don't have to be Christian to join. Everyone is welcome. We keep the focus on recovering from childhood sexual abuse. For those who struggle with the concept of God from having been spiritually abused in the past, we hope you find this a safe place to feel supported within the context of healing from the effects of both sexual and spiritual abuse. While this meeting is a Christian focus workshop, we respect everyone's spiritual beliefs per the 12 Steps and 12 Traditions of SIA and ask that shares be directly tied in to issues related to incest and recovery. To read a sample of the book: https://www.amazon.com/-/he/Shawn-Foster-ebook/dp/B0F2SBHQ6C Meeting zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87050153117?pwd=S59ECtaQomk8ObQTie3DiC8gmefocp.1 Meeting ID: 870 5015 3117 Passcode: 088019 You can also access this meeting through our other website: https://sianewyork.org/calendars--meeting-lists

name: Reclaiming Sexuality (Women/Gender Non-Conforming/Female Identifying)
notes:
7th tradition: https://siawso.org/contribute please contribute a few dollars per meeting if you can! The purpose of this workshop is to allow us to reflect on the role sexuality has played in our lives, to share the places where we feel stuck, vulnerable, confused, and even hopeless, and to get in touch with the sexual life we truly want. This workshop is different from most in SIA. Our readings and shares often speak directly about consensual physical and emotional experiences of sex, desire, boundaries, our bodies and specific anatomy; and, as fellow survivors, we work together to co-create a sensitive container for these vulnerable topics.

name: Men’s Covert Incest Group
notes:
This meeting is for men who were sexually abused as children with a focus on covert incest. Covert incest abuse occurs when the parent uses the child as a surrogate spouse. The parent’s need for companionship is met by the child. As adults, these children struggle with commitment, intimacy, and expressions of healthy sexuality. The meeting will start with reading the 12 steps of SIA, 1 tradition, and guidelines for safe sharing. The focus will be on reading literature whether from books or articles pertaining to healing from the effects of covert sexual abuse. There will be an open discussion about the topic followed by an open share that can be related to the reading or on issues related to healing from childhood sexual abuse. (Trigger warning for outside SIA literature) Starting 8-22-2026, we will be reading from the book titled: Sexual Anorexia, Overcoming Sexual Self Hatred by Patrick Carnes.

name: Surviving Family Trafficking
notes:
Surviving Family Trafficking - ZOOM Saturdays - 1:30 to 3:00 pm EST This meeting is camera-optional. We take 3 familial trafficking related topics or read from trafficking related literature or do a combination of both. Familial Trafficking is more common than people realize. Studies show that on average - about 60% of reported trafficking cases are perpetrated by family. Family traffickers include but are not limited to: parents, foster parents, step-parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, siblings, etc. Family traffickers provide perpetrators sexual access to children in the family in exchange for anything of value such as, but not limited to: money, drugs, services, status, power, etc. Note- It's not necessary to be aware of what the exchange was to determine it was trafficking. If you believe this happened to you or suspect it may have, you are welcome here. We hope you find this to be a safe place of healing and comfort. You are not alone. For any questions please email Jennifer at ncjen1611@gmail.com Meeting zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87050153117?pwd=S59ECtaQomk8ObQTie3DiC8gmefocp.1 Meeting ID: 870 5015 3117 Passcode: 088019
